title: Fix No Laser Output Issue - VertiGO Series
body_html:
No Laser Output During Processing or Pulse Test - VertiGO Series

If your VertiGO machine's laser head moves and fans spin normally, but no laser beam hits your material during a job or manual pulse test, you are dealing with an output cut-off. This troubleshooting guide walks you through diagnosing whether the issue stems from simple software settings, optical beam alignment, control board pre-ignition locks, or a hardware failure in the power supply or RF laser tube.

Problem Description

During a processing job, the laser head moves and the fans rotate normally, but no laser beam is emitted. No marks are left on the material, and the RF tube shows zero laser output.

Cause

  • Layer power settings in the file are configured too low.
  • The beam path is severely misaligned or blocked.
  • The equipment is still in its pre-ionization warm-up cycle.
  • Damaged power supply unit, damaged optical lenses, loose/damaged wiring harnesses or connectors, faulty Fan Control board port, or natural aging/failure of the RF tube.

Solution

⚠️ Important Reminder

After powering on, the RF tube undergoes a pre-ionization process for up to 45 seconds. Once completed, the machine will emit three beeps, indicating that the RF tube is fully ready for operation.

Method 1. Verify Layer Parameters

Check your software laser power settings to ensure the output percentage is not set too low, which can cause the machine to appear as though it is not firing.

Method 2. Confirm Operating Ambient Temperature

The operating ambient temperature for the laser tube must be kept strictly between 32°F and 95°F (0°C to 35°C). Operating outside this temperature range may trigger safety cutoffs or operational anomalies, resulting in no laser output from the RF tube.

Method 3. Check Direct Output at the RF Tube Aperture

Remove the rear panel of the VertiGO. Place a small piece of wood directly in front of the RF tube exit aperture. Press the Pulse button on the control panel to test for direct laser output at the source:

  • Laser output present: The fault is caused by beam path misalignment or optical lens damage. Proceed to Method 4 to calibrate the optical path.
  • No laser output: The issue lies within the RF tube itself, the wiring, or the power supply.

Method 4. Inspect Lenses and Beam Alignment

Inspect all mirrors, the beam combiner, and the focus lens along the optical path. Cracks, burns, or severe physical damage to any optic will block the laser beam from traveling to the work surface.

  • Refer to this step-by-step alignment tutorial: How to Adjust the Optical Path In Vertigo?

Method 5. Inspect the Pre-Ignition Status

If you do not hear the three beeps 45 seconds after powering on, open the rear cover and inspect the D5, D2, and D1 LED indicators on the control board:

  • Normal Status: Indicators D5, D2, and D1 should all be OFF.
  • Abnormal Status: If any LED remains lit, refer to the following diagnostic guide:
    • D5 (Solid ON): Indicates a voltage anomaly. Perform power/electrical troubleshooting.
    • D2 (Solid ON): Indicates the RF tube temperature is too high. The laser will lock out. Stop operation, wait 4–5 minutes for the RF tube to cool down, and try again.
    • D1 (Solid ON): Indicates the unit is still stuck in the pre-ignition phase. Wait a few extra minutes.

Locate the gray Ethernet network cable. Unplug both ends (at the Fan Control board and the RF tube) and firmly reconnect them. If the issue persists, swap it out with a known working Ethernet cable.

Method 6. Inspect the Power Supply Unit

Prepare a multimeter. Locate the power supply and check whether its green LED indicator is solid ON:

  • Green Light Solid ON: Use multimeter probes to measure the voltage across the +V and -V terminals. It should read 48V. An abnormal reading confirms a faulty PSU.
  • Green Light OFF: Measure the input voltage across terminals L4 and N4. It should read 220V (or 110V). If input voltage is normal but the green light remains off, the PSU is defective. If input voltage is abnormal, check the upstream main power wiring.

Method 7. Inspect Wiring and Terminal Connections

Locate the FanCtrl board. Use a multimeter to measure the voltage across the L-ON and GND terminals. It should read 5V.

With the machine powered OFF, verify that all wiring connectors on the Fan Control board are firmly seated.

Check the primary power cables (positive and negative terminals) connected to the RF tube to ensure they are securely fastened.

Method 8. Isolate and Test the RF Tube

To determine whether the fault stems from the RF tube itself or an incoming control signal, perform a short-circuit diagnostic test using a standard Ethernet cable:

1. Take a spare Ethernet cable and cut off the RJ45 crystal connector at one end.

2. Strip the insulation from wires 1, 3, and 7 (Orange-White, Green-White, Brown-White) and twist them firmly together (shorted).

Note: This modified end remains free and does NOT plug into the mainboard.

3. Plug the intact RJ45 connector on the other end directly into the network port on the RF tube.

4. Power on the machine and wait 42 seconds for the pre-ignition cycle to complete.

  • Laser Fires Normally: The RF tube is fully functional. The issue lies within the mainboard or control signal pipeline.
  • No Laser Output: The RF tube is defective and requires replacement.

 

Important Reminder:

If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
